notes: All 6 regions (1_2, 3, 4, 5, 6_8, 7) at all 11 AEPs. Transcribed from SIR 2016-5083 ver. 1.1 (April 2017): equations, MEV, AVP, SEP and n from Table 4 (report pages 20-21); variable limits from Table 5 (page 23); covariance matrices [X^T Lambda^-1 X]^-1 from Table A5 of sir20165083_appendixa.xlsx. Values were double-entered (hand transcription vs. programmatic parse of the PDF text) with zero disagreements, and cross-checked against the live NSS service (Idaho = NSS region 16, citation 39). Units: model_error_variance and avp are Table 4's MEV and AVP columns, log10 units squared, copied as printed. sep_log is derived from Table 4's SEP (percent) as sqrt(ln(1 + (SEP/100)^2)) / ln(10); the report's SEM and pseudo-R2 are not stored. Intercept is log10 of the printed power-form coefficient. AEP 0.667 and 0.429 are the report's Q67 and Q43 (1.5- and 2.33-year recurrence; NSS PK66_7AEP and PK42_9AEP). Scaled terms are stored as published, using Variable.scale/offset, so every Table A5 covariance matrix is copied as printed with no rebasing: region 4's (F/100 + 1)^b, F = LC11FOREST in percent, is log10 with scale 0.01 and offset 1, and region 7's (Emin/1,000)^b, Emin = MINBELEV in feet, is log10 with scale 0.001. Limits stay in the published units (percent, feet). Table A5's row order is the intercept followed by the variables in printed-equation order (region 4: A, F, P); for region 4 this was confirmed by MEV + mean x'Ux over Table A2's 28 region 4 sites reproducing Table 4's AVP (to 0.23% when MEV and AVP are recovered from the SEM and SEP percents), while the same check is off by a factor of 25 or more if P and F are swapped or F is taken as log10(F + 1). PRECPRIS10 is NSS's code for the report's mean annual precipitation (Table 2 lists it as PRECIP, PRISM). NSS discrepancies found while cross-checking (NSS, not this file, is wrong): region 1_2 DRNAREA maximum is 107,000 mi2 in NSS but 10,700 in Table 5; NSS reports region 6_8's SEP percentages for region 7.
